Good evening, Chair Acuff, members of the board, and members of our community. September is recognized nationally as Suicide Prevention Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness, share hope, and remind one another of the importance of the connection and care.

Established in 2008, this observance includes National Suicide Prevention Week and World Suicide Prevention Day on September the 10th. These designations reflect a nationwide commitment to ensuring the individuals and families know that support is available and that suicide is preventable.

One important advancement in recent years has been the creation of the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This national initiative reflects a growing recognition of the need for accessible mental health services. The lifeline provides free, 24-7 confidential support via call, text, chat, and it connects individuals not only with trained crisis counselors but with local mental health resources for our military families it also integrates directly with the veterans crisis line offering specialized support here in albemarle county public schools we recognize that the well-being of our students is foundational to their success to strengthen this commitment we

have implemented the help me confidential reporting system which allows families to be connected directly with our dedicated professionals including mental health support specialists school counselors, and school psychologists. I also want to acknowledge those who could not be here tonight. Their work is equally vital and their unwavering dedication continues to make a difference every single day.
